short: A brutal and prolonged military blockade undertaken by German and Finnish army groups against the Soviet city of Leningrad.
full:
In September 1941, the German Army Group North reached the outskirts of Leningrad, cutting off all land connections to the city. Rather than attempting a costly urban assault, German forces established a siege to starve the city into submission. For almost nine hundred days, the city's inhabitants endured relentless artillery bombardment and severe winter conditions with drastically reduced food rations.

Hundreds of thousands of civilians died of starvation, disease, and exposure. A fragile supply line across the frozen Lake Ladoga, known as the Road of Life, was the city's only link to the rest of the Soviet Union. The siege was finally lifted in January 1944 following a massive Soviet offensive. It remains one of the longest and deadliest sieges in human history.
